_meta.description: Static course-profile layer for Formintel. Keys are normalised course names (lowercase, letters only — matches the app/proxy normCourse()). Physical track traits only; no form data, so this never goes stale.

fields.name: Display name
fields.code: flat | jumps | both | aw (all-weather flat) | mixed-aw (AW flat + turf jumps)
fields.hand: L = left-handed, R = right-handed, S = straight/predominantly straight, F8 = figure-of-eight
fields.sharpness: 1 = very sharp/tight, 2 = sharp, 3 = fair, 4 = galloping, 5 = very galloping/stiff stamina test
fields.runIn: short | medium | long (jumps: distance from last obstacle to line)

aintree.name: Aintree
aintree.notes: National course galloping with unique fences; inner Mildmay course flat, fast and much sharper

ascot.name: Ascot
ascot.notes: Galloping, stiff finish; stamina at the trip essential

ayr.name: Ayr
ayr.notes: Fast, fair, galloping — Scotland's premier track

bangor.name: Bangor-on-Dee
bangor.notes: Sharp, flat; handy types and slick jumpers favoured

bath.name: Bath
bath.notes: Sharp bends into an uphill climb to the line; no straight sprint course quirks aside

beverley.name: Beverley
beverley.notes: Stiff uphill finish; strong low-draw bias in 5f races

brighton.name: Brighton
brighton.notes: Sharp, switchback U-shape like Epsom; agile course specialists thrive

carlisle.name: Carlisle
carlisle.notes: Stiff, testing climb home; a proper stamina track

cartmel.name: Cartmel
cartmel.notes: Very sharp holiday track but with the longest run-in in Britain (~800yds) — don't commit too soon

catterick.name: Catterick
catterick.notes: Very sharp, largely downhill; speed and a prominent position are gold

chelmsford.name: Chelmsford City
chelmsford.notes: Polytrack; fair, wide bends for an AW track

cheltenham.name: Cheltenham
cheltenham.notes: The ultimate stamina test; undulating with the famous uphill finish

chepstow.name: Chepstow
chepstow.notes: Galloping with pronounced undulations; stamina counts, especially in soft-ground jumps races

chester.name: Chester
chester.notes: Tightest circuit in Britain (~1m round); low draw and early speed are huge

doncaster.name: Doncaster
doncaster.notes: Wide, flat, galloping — form works out; fair to all run styles

downroyal.name: Down Royal
downroyal.notes: Galloping with a testing climb; genuine stamina track

downpatrick.name: Downpatrick
downpatrick.notes: Switchback, very undulating; course specialists do well

dundalk.name: Dundalk
dundalk.notes: Polytrack oval under lights; prominent racers and low draws favoured

epsom.name: Epsom Downs
epsom.notes: Unique gradients and camber; balance and agility as important as ability

exeter.name: Exeter
exeter.notes: Long, stiff, undulating — one of the toughest stamina tests outside Cheltenham

fairyhouse.name: Fairyhouse
fairyhouse.notes: Galloping and fair; home of the Irish National

fakenham.name: Fakenham
fakenham.notes: Tight, almost square circuit; course form and handiness essential

ffoslas.name: Ffos Las
ffoslas.notes: Flat, wide and galloping; can get very testing when wet

fontwell.name: Fontwell Park
fontwell.notes: Chase course is a figure-of-eight (hurdles a sharp left-handed oval); big course-specialist track

galway.name: Galway
galway.notes: Sharp with a steep climb after the last; festival handicaps favour the well-handicapped and handy

goodwood.name: Goodwood
goodwood.notes: Sharp, downland switchback; a nimble traveller's track despite the long straight

gowranpark.name: Gowran Park
gowranpark.notes: Galloping and testing, especially in winter ground

hamilton.name: Hamilton Park
hamilton.notes: Undulating with a stiff climb to the line

haydock.name: Haydock Park
haydock.notes: Flat, wide, galloping; a fair test where stamina holds up

hereford.name: Hereford
hereford.notes: Sharp-ish, mostly flat; suits handy front-runners

hexham.name: Hexham
hexham.notes: Severe undulations and a stiff climb home; proven stamina essential

huntingdon.name: Huntingdon
huntingdon.notes: Flat, fast and fair; slick jumping at pace rewarded

kelso.name: Kelso
kelso.notes: Sharp-ish but with a long uphill run-in on the hurdle course — closers get time

kempton.name: Kempton Park
kempton.notes: Flat and fair on both codes; Polytrack flat, park-style jumps course rewards fluent jumping

kilbeggan.name: Kilbeggan
kilbeggan.notes: Tight summer jumps track; handiness and course form count

killarney.name: Killarney
killarney.notes: Sharp, picturesque summer track; speed and position favoured

laytown.name: Laytown
laytown.notes: Beach racing on the strand — one meeting a year, form guide largely folklore

leicester.name: Leicester
leicester.notes: Stiff, galloping; the straight-course climb finds them out

leopardstown.name: Leopardstown
leopardstown.notes: Flat, galloping, fair — Ireland's premier dual-purpose track

limerick.name: Limerick
limerick.notes: Galloping with an uphill finish; stamina track

lingfield.name: Lingfield Park
lingfield.notes: Sharp Polytrack circuit; turf course undulating with a downhill run like a mini-Epsom

listowel.name: Listowel
listowel.notes: Sharp, flat harvest-festival track; handy types favoured

ludlow.name: Ludlow
ludlow.notes: Sharp, flat and fast; slick-jumping front-runners hard to peg back

marketrasen.name: Market Rasen
marketrasen.notes: Sharp right-handed summer-jumping hub; prominent racers and quick jumpers thrive, hold-up horses struggle

musselburgh.name: Musselburgh
musselburgh.notes: Sharp, flat and fast-drying; early pace holds well

naas.name: Naas
naas.notes: Galloping, stiff finish; a proper test that suits gallopers

navan.name: Navan
navan.notes: Galloping and testing; winter form here is a strong stamina pointer

newbury.name: Newbury
newbury.notes: Wide, flat, galloping — one of the fairest tracks in the country

newcastle.name: Newcastle
newcastle.notes: Tapeta flat course straight and fair; jumps course galloping with a stiff finish

newmarket.name: Newmarket
newmarket.notes: Rowley Mile and July Course both wide, mostly straight and stiff; the ultimate galloping test

newtonabbot.name: Newton Abbot
newtonabbot.notes: Tight, flat summer-jumping track; front-runners do very well

nottingham.name: Nottingham
nottingham.notes: Flat and galloping; fair to all

perth.name: Perth
perth.notes: Sharp, flat summer track; handiness and fast jumping rewarded

plumpton.name: Plumpton
plumpton.notes: Tight, undulating; big course-specialist and front-runner track

pontefract.name: Pontefract
pontefract.notes: Undulating with a stiff climb over the last three furlongs; stamina at the trip vital

punchestown.name: Punchestown
punchestown.notes: Galloping and fair; Ireland's championship jumps test

redcar.name: Redcar
redcar.notes: Flat, fast and galloping with a long straight

ripon.name: Ripon
ripon.notes: Sharp; draw and early pace significant, especially in sprints

roscommon.name: Roscommon
roscommon.notes: Sharp-ish summer track; prominent racers favoured

salisbury.name: Salisbury
salisbury.notes: Stiff, uphill finish; a genuine test at every trip

sandown.name: Sandown Park
sandown.notes: Galloping with the famous uphill finish; the railway fences reward bold jumping

sedgefield.name: Sedgefield
sedgefield.notes: Sharp and undulating; course specialists and handy sorts do best

sligo.name: Sligo
sligo.notes: Tight with a stiff climb to the line

southwell.name: Southwell
southwell.notes: Tapeta flat course sharp and speed-favouring; flat jumps course fair

stratford.name: Stratford-on-Avon
stratford.notes: Tight, flat, fast summer track; be handy or be beaten

taunton.name: Taunton
taunton.notes: Sharp, flat; prominent racers and quick jumpers favoured

thirsk.name: Thirsk
thirsk.notes: Sharp and fast; draw and early speed matter

thurles.name: Thurles
thurles.notes: Sharp-ish winter track that drains well; handy types favoured

tipperary.name: Tipperary
tipperary.notes: Flat and fair with a long straight for a small track

tramore.name: Tramore
tramore.notes: Very tight and undulating; a course-specialist's paradise

uttoxeter.name: Uttoxeter
uttoxeter.notes: Fair, slightly undulating; can become a slog in soft winter ground

warwick.name: Warwick
warwick.notes: Sharp with a tight final bend; fluent jumping and position count

wetherby.name: Wetherby
wetherby.notes: Flat, galloping; a fair jumps test where form holds up

wexford.name: Wexford
wexford.notes: Sharp; switched from left- to right-handed in 2015 — pre-2015 course form reads backwards

wincanton.name: Wincanton
wincanton.notes: Fast, free-draining; bold-jumping front-runners hard to catch

windsor.name: Windsor
windsor.notes: Figure-of-eight but most races use the long straight mile; effectively fair

wolverhampton.name: Wolverhampton
wolverhampton.notes: Tight Tapeta oval; draw and early position significant

worcester.name: Worcester
worcester.notes: Flat, fair summer-jumping track with long straights

yarmouth.name: Great Yarmouth
yarmouth.notes: Flat and fair; straight-mile form transfers from Newmarket

york.name: York
york.notes: Wide, flat, very galloping — the fairest big-field track in Britain

ballinrobe.name: Ballinrobe
ballinrobe.notes: Sharp summer track with an uphill finish

bellewstown.name: Bellewstown
bellewstown.notes: Sharp hilltop summer track; handiness rewarded

clonmel.name: Clonmel
clonmel.notes: Undulating with a stiff uphill finish

curragh.name: Curragh
curragh.notes: Vast, wide, galloping — Ireland's classic championship test
